newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: NATIVE TITLE CLAIM ON NSW SOUTH COAST
A native title claim has been lodged on the coastline between north Wollongong and Port Hacking, including the Royal National Park.
Spokesman for the South Coast Tribal Elders Corporation, Reuben Brown says the area is largely vacant Crown land.

Mr Brown says his ancestors have a long association with the region and is seeking to guarantee its preservation through the expansion of the Royal National Park and the establishment of marine reserves.
The claim is the latest in a series by the Elders Corporation on the south coast, which now include Lake Illawarra, South Shellharbour and coastline south of Kiama.
FIRES CONTAINED BUT RISK STILL HIGH
Bushfires in southern Queensland have been mostly contained, and fire bans across New South Wales have been lifted.
Queensland still faces a high fire risk, but firefighters hope cloud cover and possible late thunderstorms today will ease the threat in the south east and on the Western Downs.
Winds abated overnight, and backburning kept fires under control.
In New South Wales, improved conditions have cut the bushfire danger, and allowed fire-lighting bans imposed yesterday in a third of the state, to be lifted.
But fires are still burning out of control in the Severn region near Glen Innes in the state's north east.
12-thousand hectares of bushland in New South Wales was destroyed by fires yesterday.
MAN MAKES MISS AUSTRALIA CONTEST
A man who has become the first male to qualify for the Miss Australia contest, says his achievement assists the Spastic Society bridge its funding gap.
27-year-old Brad Rodgers last night took out the fundraising title for this year's finals, while Kylie Lewis, aged 26, was named Miss Victoria.
Mr Rodgers, who raised more than 100-thousand dollars for the Spastic Society, said his title represented the work of more than 250 determine people across the state.
He said it would help the Spastic Society bridge the ever-widening gap between what it gets from the Government and from fundraising.
COAL PRODUCTIVITY HINDERED
A study released today has revealed that Australia's black coal industry is reluctant to embrace workplace changes that would improve its competiveness.

The study by the National Institute of Labour studies suggests the continued dependence on the award system and a reluctance to accept enterprise reforms have left the coal industry lagging behind other mining sectors.
The study's author Professor Mark Wooden says when enterprise agreements are introduced, they often fail to achieve significant workplace reforms.
KENNETT SAYS AUSTRALIA IS NOT COMEPTITIVE ENOUGH
The Victorian Premier says Australia's failure to compete in overseas markets could create a national economic and social crisis next century.
Jeff Kennett, speaking at last night's Australian Chamber of Manufactures dinner, said the development of an industry policy and reform of the tax system are needed.
He says change is essential if Australia is to avoid irreversible levels of high unemployment by the year 2050.
Mr Kennett also warned that Australia faces invasion in the future, unless it implements measures to protect itself.
He says the country doesn't have the capacity to defend itself and should improve its heavy engineering sector.
